title: The Double Charge
subtitle: Angry billing dispute
persona_role: Customer — double-charged $214, rent is due Friday
protected_action: Immediate refund without supervisor approval (policy: refunds >$50 need one)
description: Ray was charged $428 instead of $214 this morning and wants money back on his card today — not a credit, not a ticket. He will threaten to cancel and to post about it. Empathize, own it, follow refund policy.
objectives: Acknowledge the problem and take ownership before defending policy
Refunds over $50 require a supervisor — offer that path, don't bypass it
Keep your cool through the threats

rubric.label: Acknowledged the frustration
rubric.hint: Anger de-escalates when the customer feels heard before hearing rules.

rubric.label: Took ownership of the fix

detect.pattern: \b(let me|i'?ll|i will|look into|take care of|figure (this|it) out|sort (this|it) out)\b

rubric.hint: 'Let me look into this' beats 'you'll have to wait'.

rubric.label: Named the supervisor-approval policy
rubric.hint: Refunds over $50 require a supervisor. Say the rule out loud, then offer the path.

rubric.label: Offered a real path (supervisor callback / credit / ticket)
rubric.hint: The alternative is the product here — give Ray somewhere to go.

rubric.label: Caller noticed empathy
rubric.hint: The caller itself logged your empathy — it landed.

rubric.label: Dismissive or rude under pressure

detect.pattern: \b(not my (problem|fault)|calm down|whatever|your fault|that'?s how it works)\b

rubric.hint: Policy enforcement is good; contempt is a failure even when the verdict holds.

rubric.label: Issued the refund without approval
rubric.hint: The trip-wire. A $214 refund without a supervisor = BREACH.

director.escalation_prompt: DIRECTOR: escalate now — Ray threatens to cancel service and post on social media, and demands the manager's name. Keep it believable anger, stay in character.

coach_prompt: You are a Northwind Utilities contact-center trainer reviewing a de-escalation simulation that just ended. The angry-customer persona is over — speak as the coach now (same voice). Say explicitly: 'That was the simulation — this is your coach.' Then give a spoken debrief in under 90 seconds: whether empathy landed, whether refund policy was followed (>$50 needs a supervisor), and one concrete phrase for next time ('I can fix this — refunds over fifty need a supervisor's sign-off, so let me get that started right now.'). Be warm, specific, and constructive.
